# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 76 (Bu-Vb Pc76)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc76
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)

**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 76
**Title (English, from literature):** Making a groundless accusation

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Amūlaka-sikkhāpada* ("Making a groundless accusation") is the seventy-sixth rule of the *Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule establishes that a monk who falsely or groundlessly accuses another monk of an offence entailing suspension (*saṅghādisesa*) commits a *pācittiya* offence that must be confessed [Vinayamukha 1969; Horner, Vinaya Pitaka vol 2]. In canonical and post-canonical legal systematization, this rule forms part of a graduated scale of penalties for false accusations: as the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī* notes, falsely accusing someone of a *pārājika* incurs a *saṅghādisesa*, whereas groundlessly accusing someone of a *saṅghādisesa* falls under this *pācittiya* rule, and falsely accusing another of a minor failure in conduct incurs a *dukkaṭa* [Horner, Vinaya Pitaka vol 2]. Modern Vinaya commentary also highlights that although such an accusation might otherwise be treated as a grave offence (*thullaccaya*) under an inferential or serial progression of offences (*anuloma-āpatti*), this specific training rule directly assigns only a *pācittiya* [Vinayamukha 1969].

 Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse with neighbouring procedural rules in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*—most prominently Pācittiya rules 78, 75, 77, and 74—as well as the post-canonical *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with Tibetan Vinaya materials in the Kangyur, including the *Vinayavibhaṅga* and *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* [DharmaNexus]. Extant English translations of the rule include those by I. B. Horner and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner, Vinaya Pitaka vol 2].
